chapter.title: Contributing an Add-on
chapter.para: This chapter describes what belongs in this repository, how add-on artifacts are named and published, and what a contribution is expected to include.

section.title: Where a component belongs
section.para: OpenNLP core contains the shared interfaces, published in opennlp-api, and the implementations that fit its component model without new runtime dependencies or bundled data.

An add-on implements a core interface, or supplies an independent component, when it needs additional dependencies, models, dictionaries, datasets, or a separate release cycle. Add-ons use public OpenNLP APIs; they do not duplicate them, bypass them, or rely on package-private access.
The sandbox remains the place for proofs of concept, services, and work that is not ready for an ASF release.
When an add-on needs a reusable interface that core does not have yet, propose it as a small core change and keep the implementation here.

section.title: Artifacts and packages
section.para: Each add-on module is published to Maven Central as org.apache.opennlp.addons:artifactId.

Module and artifact names describe the feature and carry no -addon suffix. Java package names describe the feature rather than the repository it is hosted in, so that a package does not have to be renamed if a component later moves into core. Each implementation package belongs to exactly one module.

Keep published Maven coordinates stable. If Maven coordinates do change, ship a relocation POM for the transition and verify that dependency resolution still works; previously published JARs stay available, and consumers otherwise face duplicate classes and split packages.

section.title: Dependencies and licensing
section.para: Keep dependencies to a minimum. A new dependency, in core or in an add-on, draws considerably more scrutiny from reviewers than an equivalent hand-written solution.

Every dependency and bundled resource needs a license that the ASF third-party licensing policy permits, and recorded provenance. A module that downloads user-selected resources documents the source, who is responsible for its license, and how integrity is verified.

section.title: What a pull request includes
section.para: Each pull request covers one module, or one focused change, and includes:

listitem.para: tests for normal and for invalid input;
a manual page with dependency and usage examples; and
a completed pull request template, including the OpenNLP version the change was verified against.

section.para: LICENSE and NOTICE are not edited by hand. The CI Master - Regenerate NOTICE workflow regenerates them from the dependency tree and opens a pull request with the result.

A contribution that depends on an unreleased core API stays in draft and documents how to build it locally. It is ready for review once it builds against a published OpenNLP artifact that contains that API.

section.title: Releases
section.para: Add-ons release on their own cadence through the regular voting process. A release records the supported OpenNLP version and verifies every module against it. A module may extend a public core interface, but it may not offer a competing replacement for one.
Moving an add-on into core is a separate decision taken on the dev list, not an automatic consequence of adoption.
